evidence.evaluation: docs/research/guest-exclusive-control.md SHA-256 f94b4728b26944bb070fa47dc09c0885c8b893f93317120d80c9e767ba4f008d and experiments/guest-exclusive-control/results.toml SHA-256 627b1187a7ff0296e5c8dde61fb23396a767772ec02fc47e9e68071b20c2c49a distinguish direct private evidence, stock inference and unknown mechanism. Changing the observation regime changed progress with identical code and private inputs: both continuous arms succeeded immediately while both stepped arms exhausted eight attempts. This is repeatability within one guest boot. Step exceptions, scheduling, trace reads and emulator/kernel mechanisms remain confounded. The result supports the earlier stock mutex retry explanation without reproducing it in Sparrow or claiming physical-instrument behavior. More stock instruction budget is not justified by this result. Input-manifest validation is performed by the launcher, not the Kotlin verifier; teardown has separate cleanup/port evidence.
evidence.next-question: Propose a separate bounded private control of hardware execution breakpoints: allow the same exclusive sequence to execute continuously and test precise terminal PC, successful result, stop metadata, availability and unexpected-stop handling. This avoids altering synchronization instructions or forcing mutex results. A later stock adaptation would retain the mapped-register boundary and explicitly account for thread coverage and intervening device accesses; a terminal state alone cannot prove an unobserved store instruction. No successor is admitted or run in this batch. Commit and push this conclusion before beginning any next experiment under the standing tasking discipline. No broader hardware semantics or device deployment are claimed.
